source.title: Directions That Don't Drift: Stiefel Manifold Routing for Transformer Attention

record.tranche_reason: The study measures training and held-out accuracy on a modular-arithmetic task, bearing on delayed generalization, but uses a different architecture and training setup from the original studies. It also tests whether Stiefel-constraining attention affects grokking.
record.gate_note: The CIFAR-10 results measure generalization but not delayed grokking, so they do not test V3. The paper's references to earlier grokking results are not rows. Grokking rows below are the study's own experiments; the targeted regularization and initialization pilot is recorded for V5, not as evidence of uninduced grokking for V1.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own modular-addition grokking experiments: (a+b) mod 97, 40% split, memorize-then-generalize timing over 5 seeds in two optimizer settings. It uses a different architecture (2-layer encoder, full batch) from Power et al. It also varies weight decay, Q/K decay exemption, circuit decay and circuit init scale. CIFAR-10 results involve no delayed generalization and do not bear on the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Missing: authors claim the Stiefel+circuit-decay pilot (B2-hi) gives the 'first stable grokking' under slingshot conditions. They also argue grokking's norm compression lies in embeddings/FFN/readout, not Q/K frames. They withdraw an earlier claim that weight decay drives the collapse cycles.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses modular addition and training/held-out accuracy, but tests Stiefel-constrained attention in a 2-layer encoder with full-batch training and additional optimizer and regularization comparisons; it is not a reproduction of the original training setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Grokking outcomes vary with seed and run; the paper reports different outcomes under β2=0.999 with no warmup versus β2=0.98 with 10-step warmup, and sensitivity to ηR and targeted circuit regularization or initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: The Stiefel constraint keeps the Q/K isometry error near 1e-5 through every slingshot collapse. With frame decay removed (A2-nwf), the error drifts to 18.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Attention routing-frame geometry is decoupled from the optimizer instabilities that occur during grokking.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors argue that fixing the Q/K frame norm leaves grokking roughly unchanged, so the norm compression driving grokking sits in the embeddings, FFN and readout.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The weight-norm mechanism of grokking is localized to circuit parameters, not the attention Q/K frames.

record.problems: The default and stabilized comparisons use five seeds per arm; the initial table includes single-run arms and identical-configuration reruns with notably different endpoints. Grokking trajectories have repeated slingshot collapses, so endpoints are not converged values. The targeted circuit-regularization pilot is single-seed, and its baseline sustained metric was not computed. The study does not vary training-set size.
record.rows_left_out: Image-benchmark accuracy and optimizer-geometry results are omitted because they do not measure delayed grokking on non-algorithmic data or another listed version. Geometric propositions are not experimental outcomes on grokking.

untested.parts: Dependence of the delay on training-set size (only the 40% split is used).
All parts: no circuit formation, memorization removal or progress measures are reported.
Delayed generalization on non-algorithmic data (CIFAR shows no delay), and weight norm or lazy-to-rich switching. Only small circuit init is tried, in one seed.
Circuit efficiency, critical dataset size, and ungrokking below it.
Floating-point softmax limits. Whether the delay vanishes once optimizer instability is controlled: the β2=0.98/warmup setting did not remove the slingshot, so this was not achieved.

missing.what: Training accuracy falls back to about 1% (chance) after memorization in all archived trajectories, in every arm. This bears on V1's claim that training accuracy stays saturated.
Five-seed default-setting results for B2m and B2-frz (shown only as bars in Figure 1 right).
Second archived B2m run at identical config ended at 75.3% (vs 60.7%).
B2-hi slingshot collapse at epoch 9 000 (training 32%) with recovery within one window.

record.verdict_notes: The Stiefel-vs-AdamW comparison confounds the decay exemption with the optimizer and norm-fixing, so it does not test V5. V7 cannot be judged because the slingshot instability was never removed. The delay persisted under β2=0.98 but shrank (median 4 985 to 2 230). All pilot results are single-seed.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not vary training-set size, so it does not test whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks. Its runs also show repeated training-accuracy collapses after memorization rather than sustained training accuracy.
It does not measure the formation of a generalizing circuit, memorizing-component removal, or continuous mechanistic progress measures.
The image benchmark does not test delayed generalization on non-algorithmic data or whether initialization scale or weight norm switches grokking on or off in that setting.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is studied.

The study tests consequences of exempting attention frames from weight decay and includes a single-seed pilot with stronger circuit decay and smaller circuit initialization. It does not measure circuit efficiency directly or test a critical dataset size or ungrokking below one.
It does not identify or compare learned algorithms across runs.

The study tests a β2 and warmup setting intended to address optimizer instability, but does not test floating-point limits in the softmax or establish that optimizer instability was successfully controlled.

rows.operation_detail: Train on modular addition and evaluate training and held-out accuracy.
rows.value: Memorized at epoch 100; grokked at epoch 3 700; held-out accuracy at epoch 20 000 was 61.1%; tail mean over epochs 15 000–20 000 was 0.55.
rows.note: The authors report repeated collapse-and-recovery cycles; they state that this run's endpoint is a sample from an oscillation.

rows.subject: A2-nwf (unconstrained; no weight decay on query/key frames), seed 0
rows.operation_detail: Remove weight decay from query and key frames while retaining circuit weight decay.
rows.measure: First and sustained held-out accuracy ≥0.95; final held-out accuracy
rows.baseline: B2-hi reached sustained ≥0.95 at epoch 2 100 and ended at 100%.
rows.value: First crossed 0.95 at epoch 2 500 but never sustained the threshold; ended at 0.9% held-out accuracy.
rows.note: This is a targeted intervention pilot, not evidence of uninduced grokking.
rows.check: Decay is removed only from the Q/K frames, with circuit decay intact. The failure to sustain does not isolate the decay-efficiency mechanism. Single seed.

rows.subject: B2-hi (Stiefel frames with increased circuit weight decay), seed 0
rows.operation_detail: Constrain query and key frames and increase weight decay on circuit parameters.
rows.measure: First and sustained held-out accuracy ≥0.95; final held-out accuracy

rows.check: Raising circuit decay to 2.0 gives a first crossing at 800 and sustained ≥0.95 from 2 100, against the B2 5-seed median of 8 785. The metrics differ (sustained vs single-crossing) and this is a single seed.
